meta.name: The Daily Reflection Tree
meta.description: A fully deterministic end-of-day reflection tool. No LLM is used at runtime. Every conversation path is determined entirely by the employee's selections. Same answers always produce the same path and the same reflection.

axes.name: Locus

poles.internal: Sees their own agency in how today unfolded — owns their response to events
poles.external: Sees today as driven by forces outside their control — circumstance, others, luck

sources: Rotter, J.B. (1954). Social learning and clinical psychology. Englewood Cliffs, NJ: Prentice-Hall.
Dweck, C.S. (2006). Mindset: The New Psychology of Success. Random House.

axes.name: Orientation

poles.contribution: Frame oriented around what they gave — discretionary effort, help, initiative
poles.entitlement: Frame oriented around what they were owed — recognition, fairness, reciprocity

sources: Campbell, W.K. et al. (2004). Psychological entitlement. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.
Organ, D.W. (1988). Organizational citizenship behavior: The good soldier syndrome. Lexington Books.

axes.name: Radius

poles.altrocentric: The frame includes others — colleagues, team, end-users, community
poles.selfcentric: The frame is primarily self-referential — own stress, goals, workload, feelings

sources: Maslow, A. (1969). The farther reaches of human nature. Journal of Transpersonal Psychology.
Batson, C.D. (2011). Altruism in humans. Oxford University Press.

state_schema.description: The full state object maintained by the agent at runtime
state_schema.answers: Record<nodeId: string, selectedOptionId: string> — every question answer stored by node ID

dominant_rules.description: How agent computes axis.dominant for condition-based routing. Applied at each decision node that references axis.dominant.
dominant_rules.axis1: internal > external → 'internal' | external > internal → 'external' | tie → 'internal' (growth-oriented tiebreak)
dominant_rules.axis2: contribution > entitlement → 'contribution' | entitlement >= contribution → 'entitlement' (surfaces it for reflection)

interpolation_rules.description: Placeholders in 'text' fields are resolved by the agent at render time from state
syntax: { nodeId.label }    → short label of the option selected at that question node
{ nodeId.answer }   → full text of the option selected at that question node
{ axis1.dominant }  → computed dominant pole string for axis 1
{ axis1.label }     → human-readable label resolved from summary_data lookup table
{ axis1.summary }   → summary sentence resolved from summary_data lookup table
{ closing_insight } → text of the first matching entry in closing_insights
{ nodeId.reflection_label }   → the reflection_label field of the selected option at nodeId (must be defined on that node's options)
{ nodeA.reflection_label|nodeB.reflection_label }  → pipe-fallback: resolve nodeA if visited, else nodeB. Used when a node is reachable from two mutually exclusive question paths.

node_types.start: Opens the session. Displays text. No input. Auto-advances to 'next'.
node_types.question: Displays text and 3–5 fixed options. Waits for employee selection. Records answer to state.answers[nodeId]. Applies signal from selected option to state tallies. Auto-advances to 'next'.
node_types.decision: Invisible to employee. Evaluates 'routing' conditions in order against current state. Advances to the first matching target. If no condition matches, advance to 'default_target'.
node_types.reflection: Displays reframe text derived from the path taken. Employee reads and presses Continue. Auto-advances to 'next'.
node_types.bridge: A short transitional sentence between axes. Displayed briefly. Auto-advances to 'target' (may cross tree hierarchy).
node_types.summary: End-of-session synthesis. Resolves all interpolation placeholders. Employee reads their personalized reflection summary. Advances to 'next'.
node_types.end: Closes the session. No further interaction.

routing_condition_syntax.description: Conditions used inside routing arrays on decision nodes
examples: INTRO_Q.answer == 'A'                   → true if employee selected option A at INTRO_Q
INTRO_Q.answer in ['A', 'B']             → true if selected option is A or B
axis1.dominant == 'internal'             → true if computed dominant for axis1 is 'internal'
axis1.internal >= axis1.external         → true if internal tally is at least as high as external
A1_Q2_EXT.answer == 'C'                  → exact option match on a specific node
axis3.altrocentric > 0   → true if altrocentric tally is at least 1 (raw tally check, used where dominant tiebreak would mask a genuine flash)
axis3.altrocentric == 0  → true if altrocentric tally is exactly zero (used to confirm zero other-awareness)
axis2.contribution == axis2.entitlement  → true if both axis2 tallies are equal (tie case)

summary_data.description: Lookup table for summary node interpolation. Agent resolves axis labels and summary sentences from state.axisN.dominant.

internal.label: more internal
internal.summary: You saw your hand in how things went. That's not a personality trait — it's a practiced stance.

external.label: more external
external.summary: A lot of today felt like it was happening to you. Somewhere in there, though, you were still making calls.

contribution.label: contribution-oriented
contribution.summary: You gave beyond what was required. Others may not have noticed — but the effect was real.

entitlement.label: return-focused
entitlement.summary: Your attention went to what you were getting — or not getting. Worth seeing clearly, without judgment.

altrocentric.label: outward-facing
altrocentric.summary: Others were genuinely in your frame today. That's the raw material of meaning.

selfcentric.label: self-focused
selfcentric.summary: Today's frame was mostly your own situation. Tomorrow, you might try widening the lens by one person.

closing_insights.text: You showed up with agency, gave without keeping score, and kept others in your view. Days like this are rare. Let yourself notice it.
Today was a survival day — and you got through it. The fact that you're here, looking at it honestly, is itself a form of agency. That counts.
You acted with purpose and gave real effort. The next step might be letting some of that extend outward — who else benefited today, even indirectly?
You kept your footing today — that matters. The question for tomorrow: where can some of that steadiness flow outward toward others?
Even when things didn't feel in your control, you still gave and stayed connected to others. That's a kind of grace under pressure.
You gave effort despite the headwinds — and that matters. The frame was still mostly your own today. Notice: who else was carrying something similar?
Even though today felt out of your hands and the return felt uneven, you still held others in mind. That's not nothing. Agency and generosity can return even from here.
You navigated the day with real clarity of action and kept others in view. The thread to pull: did the gap between what you gave and what you received actually close today?
Every day has these three layers — how you responded, what you gave, and who was in your view. You looked at all three tonight. That's where growth starts.

nodes.text:
Good evening.

This is your space — no performance, no scoring, no judgment.

You'll move through a short reflection on how today actually went. There are no right answers. The only thing that matters is that you pick the option that's genuinely true for you.

It takes about five minutes.
nodes.parents_note: Root node — session entry point. Has no parent.

nodes.text: Let's start without overthinking it. If today had a weather report, what would it say?

options.label: sunny
options.text: Sunny — things moved, and I moved with them

options.label: overcast
options.text: Overcast — got through it, nothing spectacular

options.label: stormy
options.text: Stormy — real turbulence today

options.label: foggy
options.text: Foggy — couldn't quite see where I was going

nodes.note: Routes lighter days (A, B) to a question about what drove success. Routes harder days (C, D) to a question about the first response to difficulty.

nodes.text: You said today felt {INTRO_Q.label}. Looking back at how you moved through it — what felt most in your control?

options.label: prepared
options.text: I prepared — it didn't happen by accident

options.label: team
options.text: The team came through and we built momentum together

options.label: lucky
options.text: Honestly, timing and circumstances worked in my favor

options.label: adapted
options.text: I stayed flexible when the plan changed

nodes.text: You said today felt {INTRO_Q.label}. When things got difficult, what was your first move?

options.label: controlled
options.text: I looked for what I could still control in the situation

options.label: waited
options.text: I waited for things to settle before acting

options.label: pushed
options.text: I pushed forward even though the path wasn't clear

options.label: blocked
options.text: I felt blocked — it was hard to see a way through

nodes.note: Routes to INT follow-up if answer showed agency (A, B, D). Routes to EXT follow-up if answer showed external attribution (C).
Routes to INT follow-up if first response showed agency (A, C). Routes to EXT follow-up if response was passive or blocked (B, D).

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A1_D1_LIGHT (options A,B,D) or A1_D1_HEAVY (options A,C)
nodes.text: Think of one deliberate decision you made today — even a small one. What were you protecting or building when you made it?

options.label: integrity
options.text: My own standards — I wasn't willing to cut corners

options.label: trust
options.text: The trust someone placed in me
options.reflection_label: protecting trust someone placed in you

options.label: goal
options.text: A goal I've been working toward for a while

options.label: reacting
options.text: I'm not sure — I was reacting more than choosing today

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A1_D1_LIGHT (option C) or A1_D1_HEAVY (options B,D)
nodes.text: When the situation felt out of your hands, what did you do with that feeling?

options.label: vented
options.text: I vented — it needed to get out
options.reflection_label: let it out — and then kept going

options.label: waited
options.text: I stepped back and let someone else take the lead
options.reflection_label: sat with it and waited for the pressure to ease

options.label: found
options.text: I found one small thing I could still do
options.reflection_label: found one small thing you could still act on

options.label: detached
options.text: I felt stuck — I couldn't find a way through and didn't move forward
options.reflection_label: stepped back and decided some things weren't worth fighting

nodes.note: Checks accumulated axis1 tally after both Q1 and Q2 on the internal-entry path.
If the employee found one thing they could do (C), they showed a flash of agency on the external path — route to MIX. Otherwise, route to full external reflection.

nodes.text:
You kept a hand on the wheel today — you were {A1_Q2_INT.reflection_label}.

That's not a personality type. It's a practiced stance. Agency isn't about controlling outcomes; it's about owning your response to whatever comes. You did that today.

A lot of today felt like it was happening to you — and sometimes that's simply true.

You {A1_Q2_EXT.reflection_label}. That's still a choice, even if it didn't feel like one at the time. Somewhere in today, you were making calls — the question is just whether you noticed them as yours.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A1_D2_INT (external>internal on INT path) or A1_D2_EXT (option C — flash of agency on EXT path)
nodes.text:
Today was a mixed picture — parts felt in your hands, parts didn't.

At some point you were {A1_Q2_INT.reflection_label|A1_Q2_EXT.reflection_label}. That's usually the honest truth. The question isn't whether you controlled everything — it's whether you noticed where you did have a choice, even a small one.
nodes.interpolation_note: The placeholder {A1_Q2_INT.reflection_label|A1_Q2_EXT.reflection_label} uses pipe-fallback syntax: resolve A1_Q2_INT.reflection_label if that node was visited; otherwise resolve A1_Q2_EXT.reflection_label. Exactly one of these two nodes will always be in the conversation path.

nodes.text: Good. Now let's shift the lens — from how you responded, to what you gave.
Alright. You said today felt {INTRO_Q.label}, and a lot of it landed on you. Let's look at what you brought to others anyway.
Let's look at something different now — not how you responded, but what you gave.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from all three BRIDGE_1_2 variants (A, B, C) via their 'target' field
nodes.text: Think about your interactions today. Which of these feels most true?

options.label: helped
options.text: I helped someone with something that wasn't my job to fix
options.reflection_label: helped someone past the edge of your own responsibilities

options.label: unequal
options.text: I did my work well — but felt others weren't pulling equal weight
options.reflection_label: felt the weight of uneven effort

options.label: stepped-in
options.text: I noticed a gap and stepped into it before anyone asked
options.reflection_label: spotted a gap and stepped into it

options.label: unnoticed
options.text: I worked hard and felt like it went largely unnoticed
options.reflection_label: did solid work and felt like it landed in silence

nodes.note: Routes to contribution follow-up (A,C) or entitlement follow-up (B,D).

nodes.text: What made you reach beyond your own workload today?

options.label: obvious
options.text: I saw someone struggling and it was obvious what to do

options.label: quiet-right
options.text: I knew it was the right thing, even if no one would notice

options.label: hoped
options.text: I hoped it would be recognized or returned down the line

options.label: right-person
options.text: The team needed it and I was the right person in that moment

nodes.text: When you felt under-recognized or like effort wasn't distributed fairly — what did that lead you to do?

options.label: held-level
options.text: I kept showing up at the same level regardless

options.label: dialled-back
options.text: I matched my effort to what the situation seemed to call for

options.label: spoke-up
options.text: I made my contribution visible — named it or asked for feedback

options.label: stayed-in
options.text: I stayed in the frustration for most of the day

nodes.note: Uses accumulated axis2 tally after both questions on the contribution-entry path. dominant_rule: contribution > entitlement → 'contribution', else → 'entitlement'.
Uses accumulated axis2 tally after both questions on the entitlement-entry path. If employee chose A or C, they may have crossed to contribution-dominant.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A2_D2_CONTRIB or A2_D2_ENTITLE when contribution is dominant
nodes.text:
You {A2_Q1.reflection_label} today — and that kind of move doesn't show up in any job description.

Most people operate inside the exact boundary of their role and call it done. Stepping beyond that — especially when it isn't visible or rewarded — is how teams actually hold together.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A2_D2_CONTRIB or A2_D2_ENTITLE when entitlement is dominant
nodes.text:
You {A2_Q1.reflection_label} today — and that feeling is worth sitting with honestly.

Before moving on: is there something you contributed that you might be undervaluing? Sometimes the things we give without fanfare don't even register in our own minds as 'contributions.'
Now let's zoom out even further — from what you gave, to who was in your view today.
Let's step back one more time — from what you felt you received, to what others around you experienced today.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from BRIDGE_2_3_A or BRIDGE_2_3_B via their 'target' field
nodes.text: When you picture the most significant moment of your day, who else is in that picture?

options.label: colleague
options.text: A specific colleague whose situation I was aware of

options.label: end-user
options.text: The person at the other end of our work — user, client, or community

options.label: my-team
options.text: My immediate team — we were navigating something together

options.label: just-me
options.text: Mostly just me — I was working through something on my own

nodes.note: Routes to self-centric follow-up if the frame was self-only (A). Routes to altrocentric follow-up if others were in the picture (B, C, D).

nodes.text: When the day ended and you stepped back even slightly — was there a moment where someone else's situation crossed your mind?

options.label: colleague-thought
options.text: Yes — I thought about how a specific colleague was holding up
options.reflection_label: a colleague crossing your mind — wondering how they were holding up

options.label: user-thought
options.text: Yes — I wondered how our work actually lands for the people receiving it
options.reflection_label: a moment of wondering how your work actually lands for the people receiving it

options.label: too-in-head
options.text: Not really — I was too deep in my own situation to go there
options.reflection_label: too deep in your own situation to go there

options.label: noticed-no-capacity
options.text: I noticed something but didn't have the capacity to engage with it
options.reflection_label: something on the edge of your awareness — but without the capacity to go toward it

nodes.text: Thinking about the people you just mentioned — did anything shift for them today because you were there?

options.label: saw-it
options.text: I think so — I could see it in how they responded

options.label: tried
options.text: Maybe — I can't be sure, but I tried to be present for them

options.label: just-right
options.text: I wasn't tracking the effect — I just did what felt right

options.label: caught-in-own
options.text: Probably not — I got caught in my own things and lost the thread

nodes.note: After two axis3 questions on the self-centric entry path (A3_Q1=A, selfcentric=1 at entry). Uses RAW TALLY (not dominant) because tiebreaks would always resolve to selfcentric: if employee showed ANY altrocentric flash at Q2 (options A or B → altrocentric=1), route to MIX. If employee gave no altrocentric signal at all (options C or D → altrocentric=0), route to SELF.
After two axis3 questions via the altrocentric entry path. If employee chose D (lost the thread), tally is 1:1 — selfcentric tiebreak per dominant_rule → selfcentric → MIX reflection.

nodes.text:
Today's frame was mostly your own — and sometimes that's genuinely all you have to give.

You noticed {A3_Q2_SELF.reflection_label}. Here's one thing to carry into tomorrow: is there one person in your orbit who you know is carrying something right now? Not to fix it. Just to notice them. That's where the radius starts to expand.

Others were genuinely in your view today — not as obstacles or background, but as real people with real situations.

That orientation — the awareness that your work and presence touch actual people — is where meaning tends to live. You found some of that today.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from: (a) A3_D2_SELF when employee showed any altrocentric flash (options A or B at A3_Q2_SELF → axis3.altrocentric > 0). (b) A3_D2_OTHER when employee lost the thread (option D at A3_Q2_OTHER → 1:1 tally → selfcentric dominant).
nodes.text:
You moved between self-focus and other-awareness today — and that's the honest version of most days.

The capacity to step outside your own frame, even briefly, is what separates a manageable day from a meaningful one. You did it, at least in part. That's worth something.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A3_R_SELF, A3_R_OTHER, or A3_R_MIX
nodes.note: All placeholders resolved from state at render time using summary_data lookup table and closing_insights array. closing_insight resolves to the first matching condition in closing_insights, evaluated top-to-bottom. 'default' matches always.

nodes.text: See you tomorrow.

nodes.parents_note: Reached from A2_D2_CONTRIB or A2_D2_ENTITLE when axis2 tally is exactly tied (1:1)
nodes.text:
You gave something today — and there was also a moment where the return mattered to you.

That's the honest version of most working days. The question isn't which one dominated. It's whether you noticed both — the giving and the wanting. You did.
